text: I've done a reasonable amount of yacht crewing on sailing passages in the North Sea and did have one experience where the weather felt comparable to the storm in the film. I was about 16 at the time on a 72ft/22m yacht with a crew of about 16 people split into two groups doing four-hour watches. Biggest sustained adrenaline rush of my life and definitely the most dangerous conditions I've ever been in - three of us had to crawl up to the bow at one point to take down one of the headsails in 10-metre waves, it was like being on a giant rollercoaster plunging down into the abyss during each trough. We were completely flattened on the deck and clinging on for dear life as the spray and bow-waves were breaking over us. This was with lifejackets, oilskins, and safety harnesses - I cannot imagine how hard it would have been in the old days having to go up into the rigging to take down topsails where you're being thrown around 20x more at that height and having to do it with no safety equipment or proper gear on slippery wood with no real grip and loose rigging ropes. Weirdly I'd probably find it more scary now because as a teenager I just had faith that everyone knew what they were doing and were in control of the situation - where now I feel I'd be a lot less confident in the people around me to some degree!
